blurb: In the fragment form of a `context` (the header with no braces), the `consumes` clauses come straight after the `uses` lines, before any `type` or `fn`, so a unit's dependencies are all stated at the top. Move the `consumes` line up. `uses` and `exports` follow the same rule, as `bynk.parse.uses_after_decls` and `bynk.parse.exports_after_decls`.
example:
context shop.orders
type Id = String
consumes shop.payment            // ✗ a declaration comes first

context shop.orders
consumes shop.payment            // ✓ clauses straight after the header
type Id = String
